issues.title: `AxiosError.prototype.toJSON()` can OOM when config includes an `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent`
issues.author: skrtheboss

comments.body:
Verified on current `master` (`84a9f3b`, v1.20.0): this looks **fixed** by the config-walk hardening in #11141 (`d19040b`) — `AxiosError.prototype.toJSON()` now snapshots `config` through a cycle-safe visitor instead of deep-walking agent internals.

Reproduction attempt of the original scenario on master: local server returning 500, shared `http.Agent`, 10 warm-up requests to populate sockets, then 25 concurrent failures each passed through `error.toJSON()` + `JSON.stringify` under a **256 MB heap cap**:

```
RESULT OK toJSON total length: 187440   (~7.5KB per error, no growth across requests)
```

No heap exhaustion and the serialized payload stays bounded. Could you retest on v1.20.0? If you still see unbounded growth in your setup, a standalone repro (axios version + Node version) would help pin what differs.

issues.title: fetch adapter: response-stream capability probe leaks an uncancelled ReadableStream
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

The fetch adapter's `supportsResponseStream` capability probe creates a `ReadableStream` and never cancels it, leaking one pending promise per module realm.

This is the sibling of #7515, which fixed the same defect in the `supportsRequestStream` probe. That fix shipped in 1.14.0; the response probe was not covered and still leaks in 1.20.0.

```js
// lib/adapters/fetch.js
const supportsResponseStream =
  isResponseSupported &&
  isReadableStreamSupported &&
  test(() => utils.isReadableStream(new Response('').body));   // never cancelled
```

`new Response('').body` creates a `ReadableStream` whose internal pull pipeline is set up but never consumed or cancelled, so its pull promise stays pending for the lifetime of the realm — the mechanism described in #7515.

## Reproduction

https://github.com/bdcarr/axios-fetch-probe-leak

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test        # vitest run --detect-async-leaks
```

The readme has more details about how the repro works, and a script to test before/after the proposed fix.

## Impact at scale

One leak per module realm means one per test file. On the 256-file suite in which I encountered this issue, counting only leaks whose stack originates in axios:

| axios | axios-attributed leaks |
| --- | --- |
| 1.13.2 (before #7515) | 182 |
| 1.20.0 (after #7515) | 89 |
| 1.20.0 + the change below | 4 |

Roughly one per file in each case — 1.13.2 leaks both probes, 1.20.0 only this one.

## Proposed fix

Mirror #7515: keep a reference to the probe body and cancel it once the capability has been read. With this applied the repro reports no leaks and the 256-file suite drops from 89 axios-attributed leaks to 4.

Worth doing the cleanup as an explicitly best-effort helper shared with the request probe, rather than the bare `probeBody.cancel()` the request probe uses today:

```js
const cancelProbeBody = (body) => {
  if (body == null) {
    return;
  }

  try {
    const cancelled = body.cancel();

    if (cancelled && isFunction(cancelled.then)) {
      cancelled.then(undefined, () => {});
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // Ignored: an uncancellable probe body only leaks, it is still a valid body.
  }
};
```

`isReadableStream` is a `toStringTag` check rather than a structural one, so a custom `env.Request`/`env.Response` can expose a stream-like body with no working `cancel`. Two things fall out of that, and both apply to the existing request probe as well as this one:

- a `cancel()` that throws synchronously escapes into `test()`, which turns it into `false`. So the naive fix silently downgrades a capability that was previously detected as supported.
- a `cancel()` that rejects produces an unhandled rejection, since the returned promise is dropped.

I checked both against Node 22. A native `new Response('').body.cancel()` always fulfils, so this only bites custom or polyfilled implementations, but `env.Response` is a supported injection point so it seems worth guarding.

## Environment

```
axios     1.20.0 (present since the probe was introduced; 1.13.2 leaks both probes)
Adapter   fetch
Vitest    4.1.11
Node      v22.16.0
OS        macOS 26.6.2 arm64
```

Here is your AI disclosure: :surfer: :)
